items.title: Free, Open Source StemDeck Stem Separator For Linux, Mac & Windows
items.excerpt: StemDeck is a free, open-source stem extraction platform that isolates vocals, drums, bass, piano and guitar for practice, transcription, remixing and creative audio workflows. It runs locally on Linux, macOS and Windows.
items.why: Free open-weights-style separation moves a core AI production step off paid cloud services and onto the producer's own machine.

items.title: Free Generative Sequencer For iPad & Mac, Organismi OR-1
items.excerpt: Organismi Instruments OR-1 is a free generative MIDI sequencer for iPad and Mac that creates "patterns that breathe on their own," evolving material algorithmically rather than from fixed step programming.
items.why: Generative composition as a free everyday tool — a concrete shift in how ideas get sketched, not an AI-industry headline.

items.title: Dr Dre has words for those who oppose the use of AI in music: "You sound like the person that would have been against the drum machine"
items.excerpt: Dr Dre says he is actively using AI in production and compares resistance to it with earlier panic over drum machines and synthesizers, drawing sharp pushback from parts of the industry.
items.why: A canonical producer publicly normalising AI in the studio — a marker for how quickly the craft norm is moving.

items.title: AI Remix Platform Hook Scores 'Landmark' Universal Music Deal
items.excerpt: AI remix and mashup platform Hook signed a licensing agreement with Universal Music, with attribution and artist control written into the deal — opening licensed remixing of major-label catalogue to everyday creators.
items.why: Licensed AI remixing of major-label catalogue changes what fans and creators are legally allowed to make.

items.title: The End of the Definitive Recording
items.excerpt: An argument that recording is shifting from fixed, definitive versions to adaptive, generative experiences reshaped per listener and context by AI systems.
items.why: Directly challenges the master-recording as a design object — what does 'finished' mean when playback is generative?

items.title: Universal and Sony file amended Suno lawsuit after judge gives all clear to add stream ripping claims
items.excerpt: A judge cleared UMG and Sony to add claims that Suno acquired training data by stream-ripping YouTube; the majors have now filed the amended complaint.
items.why: The one legal item today: how training data was obtained is becoming the decisive question for every generative music tool.

items.title: Voxis from CEDAR Audio
items.excerpt: CEDAR Audio's Voxis is a low-latency voice isolator optimised for live environments, pulling speech and vocals out of troublesome background noise in real time.
items.why: Real-time source separation moving from offline post to the live console — latency is the design constraint that just fell.

items.title: MiniMax Releases MiniMax-Music3: An Open-Weights Music Model Generating Complete Five-Minute Songs
items.excerpt: MiniMax-Music3 generates five-minute songs from lyrics plus a structured caption, shipping with open weights, 32kHz stereo output and permission for commercial use.
items.why: Off-list exception: no allowed-domain music outlet covered this open-weights, commercially usable full-song model — a direct alternative to closed Suno/Udio pipelines.

items.title: How Each Music Listening Platform Is Treating AI Music (Updating)
items.excerpt: A running tracker of platform policy on AI music — from Bandcamp and iHeartRadio bans to Spotify's "AI Persona" badges, Apple Music's "Made With AI" labels and Tidal's refusal to monetise AI tracks.
items.why: One map of every distribution gate an AI-assisted release now has to pass — directly affects how work gets shipped.

items.title: Billboard Affirms Commitment to Transparency Around AI-Generated Music
items.excerpt: Billboard commits to identifying songs on its charts that use AI, setting out how it will flag AI involvement across its charts and coverage.
items.why: Chart-level disclosure turns 'did you use AI?' into a metadata field creators must answer at release.
